---
title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:

---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch config
description: Configure how a route segment is prefetched during client navigation.

---

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
> - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`.

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.

> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
> - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`.

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant. 00018| 00019| When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough. 00020| 00021| > **Good to know**: 00022| > 00023| > - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. 00024| > - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error. 00025| > - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled. 00026| 00027| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher 00028| export const instant = true 00029| 00030| export default function Page() { 00031| return
...
00032| } 00033| ``` 00034| 00035| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher 00036| export const instant = true 00037| 00038| export default function Page() { 00039| return
...
00040| } 00041| ``` 00042| 00043| ## Reference 00044| 00045| The export accepts: 00046| 00047| - **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay. 00048| - **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)). 00049| - An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level). 00050| 00051| ### `level` 00052| 00053| Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment. 00054| 00055| ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 00056| export const instant = { 00057| level: 'warning', 00058| } 00059| ``` 00060| 00061| - **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected. 00062| 00063| In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`. 00064| 00065| When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults). 00066| 00067| ### Disabling instant 00068| 00069| Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it. 00070| 00071| This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`. 00072| 00073| ```tsx filename="app/tabs/layout.tsx" 00074| export const instant = false 00075| ``` 00076| 00077| ```tsx filename="app/tabs/[tab]/page.tsx" 00078| export const instant = true 00079| ``` 00080| 00081| Navigations from outside into a tab are allowed to block at the layout. Navigations between tabs are validated for instant UI. 00082| 00083| You don't need to add `false` to ancestors of an instant page just because they do something blocking — a higher-up `instant = true` doesn't force its descendants to validate, and leaving an ancestor unconfigured is fine. Reach for `false` only when you've configured a deeper page as instant and need to exempt navigations that pass through a blocking ancestor. 00084| 00085| ### Disabling static shell validation 00086| 00087| Cache Components also validates that each page in your app produces a non-empty static shell at prerender time. To opt a route out of this validation, ensure the highest `instant` config in the route's tree is `false` — a `false` higher in the tree takes precedence over any deeper `true` for the static-shell check. 00088| 00089| Setting `false` on the root layout disables static shell validation for the entire app. Place the `false` as low as possible — only as high as needed to cover the routes you want to opt out — so the rest of the app keeps validating. 00090| 00091| ## How validation works 00092| 00093| `instant` triggers validation at every shared layout boundary in the route. Validation runs during development (on page loads and HMR updates) and surfaces errors in the dev error overlay. 00094| 00095| Each error identifies the component that would block navigation. The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `` boundary. 00096| 00097| ## How `instant` differs from `ensureStatic` 00098| 00099| `instant` validates whether a navigation shows UI immediately. [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) requires selected server-rendered output to be static instead of rendered for each request. A route can be fully static and still block a navigation, for example when a Client Component loads data in the browser. 00100| 00101| ## Configuring validation defaults 00102| 00103| By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`. 00104| 00105| ```js filename="next.config.js" 00106| module.exports = { 00107| experimental: { 00108| instantInsights: { 00109| validationLevel: 'warning', 00110| }, 00111| }, 00112| } 00113| ``` 00114| 00115| The supported levels are: 00116| 00117| - **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only). 00118| - **`'manual-warning'`**: Only segments with an explicit `instant` are validated, at warning level (dev only). 00119| 00120| Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely. 00121| 00122| > **Good to know**: 00123| > 00124| > - The framework default may change in future versions to opt users into higher levels of validation. Because this feature is experimental, that change is not considered a breaking change. To pin a specific behavior, set `validationLevel` explicitly. 00125| > - Framework-synthesized error routes (`/_global-error`, `/_not-found`) are excluded from implicit validation. To validate them, opt in explicitly with `instant`. 00126| 00127| ## Inspecting loading states 00128| 00129| The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 00130| 00131| ```js filename="next.config.js" 00132| module.exports = { 00133| cacheComponents: true, 00134| } 00135| ``` 00136| 00137| Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then turn on **Pause on navigations**. While the toggle is on: 00138| 00139| - Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in. 00140| - Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route. 00141| 00142| When the UI is frozen, click **Resume** to let the current navigation finish. The toggle stays on, so the next refresh or link click pauses too. Turn it off when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation. 00143| 00144| ## Testing instant navigation 00145| 00146| The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. The testing API is available automatically in development. For a production build, enable [`experimental.exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild) in the test build. See the [guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for a full example. 00147| 00148| ```typescript 00149| import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 00150| ``` 00151| 00152| {/* TODO: remove when fixed and from prod-docs-release */} 00153| 00154| ## Known issue: shared cookie across projects 00155| 00156| The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues. 00157| 00158| > **Good to know:** This will be fixed as part of stabilizing the feature. 00159| 00160| ## TypeScript 00161| 00162| ```tsx 00163| type InstantConfig = 00164| | true 00165| | false 00166| | { 00167| level?: 'warning' 00168| } 00169| 00170| export const instant: InstantConfig = true 00171| ``` 00172| 00173| ## Version History 00174| 00175| | Version | Changes | 00176| | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 00177| | `v16.3.0` | `instant` export stabilized, replacing `unstable_instant` (Cache Components only). | 00178| (End of file - total 178 lines)

---
title: instant
description: Configure instant navigation validation for a route segment.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation

    - app/getting-started/revalidating

---

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

---
title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.
nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Learn more about the APIs and concepts used in this guide.
  links:

    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022|

It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.

00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00088| 
00089| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00090| 
00091| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
00092| 
00093| ```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
00094| import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
00095| import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099| 
00100|   await instant(page, async () => {
00101|     const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()
00103|     await link.click()
00104|     await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
00105| 
00106|     await expect(
00107|       page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00108|     ).toBeVisible()
00109|     await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
00110|   })
00111| })
00112| ```
00113| 
00114| Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
00115|

00123| // After
00124| <Link href="/about">About</Link>
00125| ```

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:

00474| ## Prefetching URL data
00475| 
00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) resolves it ahead of the click for links with `prefetch={true}`, at the cost of a server invocation per prefetchable link. To make the content resolvable at prefetch time, cache it behind the read with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For a search page that reads `searchParams`:

nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching

---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. 00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.

00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.

00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.

00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. 00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321|

00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher

00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332|

00335|    }

00337|

00013| ---
00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

00093| ```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}

00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099|

00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()

00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00288| 
00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00294|     snippets={[
00295|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00296|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00297|     ]}
00298|   />
00299|   <FixCard
00300|     group="disable"
00301|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00302|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00303|     snippets={[
00304|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00306|       { text: '</Link>' },
00307|     ]}
00308|   />
00309| </FixCardGrid>
00310| 
00311| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00312| 
00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00339|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {
00343|      return <Dashboard />
00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00351| 
00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00353| 
00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00356| ```
00357| 
00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00361| 
00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. 00365| 
00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00370|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"

00379|     title="Allow blocking route"
00380|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"

00394| export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00395|   const { slug } = await params
00396|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00397|   return (
00398|     <ProductLayout>
00399|       <Details product={product} />
00400|     </ProductLayout>
00401|   )
00402| }
00403| ```
00404| 
00405| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00409|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00410|   return (
00411|     <ProductLayout>
00412|       <Details product={product} />
00413|     </ProductLayout>
00414|   )
00415| }
00416| ```
00417| 
00418| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher

00420| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00421| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00424|   return (
00425|     <ProductLayout>
00426|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00427|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00428|       </Suspense>
00429|     </ProductLayout>
00430|   )
00431| }
00432| ```
00433| 
00434| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00435| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00436| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00437| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00438| 
00439| export default function Page({ params }) {
00440|   return (
00441|     <ProductLayout>
00442|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00443|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00444|       </Suspense>
00445|     </ProductLayout>
00446|   )
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| The child awaits the promise inside the boundary:
00451| 
00452| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher
00453| export async function ProductDetails({
00454|   params,
00455| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
00456|   const { slug } = await params
00457|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00458|   return <Details product={product} />
00459| }
00460| ```
00461| 
00462| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.js" switcher

00464|   const { slug } = await params

00470| Everything outside the boundary stays in the shared App Shell, and only the URL-specific region renders per navigation. Load or navigate to the route again to confirm the insight is gone and the page still paints meaningful UI.
00471| 
00472| > **Good to know**: A `params` or `searchParams` read inside [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) surfaces as [URL data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) instead.

00474| ## Prefetching URL data
00475| 
00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. 00548|   )
00549| }

title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00304| - `false`: Prefetching will never happen both on entering the viewport and on hover.
00305| 
00306| > **With Partial Prefetching enabled** ([`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching)): the default changes. `auto` prefetches the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) (the route's static and cached content) instead of the full page. See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the full behavior change.
00307| 
00308| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00309| import Link from 'next/link'
00310| 
00311| export default function Page() {
00312|   return (
00313|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00314|       Dashboard
00315|     </Link>
00316|   )
00317| }
00318| ```

00320| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00321| import Link from 'next/link'

00326|       Dashboard
00327|     </Link>
00328|   )
00329| }
00330| ```

00332| </AppOnly>

00453| ### `onNavigate`
00454| 
00455| An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a `preventDefault()` method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed.
00456| 
00457| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00458| import Link from 'next/link'
00459| 
00460| export default function Page() {
00461|   return (
00462|     <Link
00463|       href="/dashboard"
00464|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00465|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00466|         console.log('Navigating...')
00467| 
00468|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00469|         // e.preventDefault()
00470|       }}
00471|     >
00472|       Dashboard
00473|     </Link>
00474|   )
00475| }
00476| ```
00477| 
00478| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00479| import Link from 'next/link'
00480| 
00481| export default function Page() {
00482|   return (
00483|     <Link
00484|       href="/dashboard"
00485|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00486|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00487|         console.log('Navigating...')
00488| 
00489|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00490|         // e.preventDefault()
00491|       }}
00492|     >
00493|       Dashboard
00494|     </Link>
00495|   )
00496| }
00497| ```
00498| 
00499| > **Good to know**: While `onClick` and `onNavigate` may seem similar, they serve different purposes. `onClick` executes for all click events, while `onNavigate` only runs during client-side navigation. Some key differences:
00500| >
00501| > - When using modifier keys (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` + Click), `onClick` executes but `onNavigate` doesn't since Next.js prevents default navigation for new tabs.
00502| > - External URLs won't trigger `onNavigate` since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.
00503| > - Links with the `download` attribute will work with `onClick` but not `onNavigate` since the browser will treat the linked URL as a download.

00537| ## Examples

00543| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00544| 
00545| When linking to [dynamic segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can use [template literals and interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) to generate a list of links. For example, to generate a list of blog posts:
00546| 
00547| ```tsx filename="app/blog/post-list.tsx" switcher
00548| import Link from 'next/link'
00549| 
00550| interface Post {
00551|   id: number
00552|   title: string
00553|   slug: string
00554| }
00555| 
00556| export default function PostList({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
00557|   return (
00558|     <ul>
00559|       {posts.map((post) => (
00560|         <li key={post.id}>
00561|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00562|         </li>
00563|       ))}
00564|     </ul>
00565|   )
00566| }
00567| ```

00847| ### Disable scrolling to the top of the page
00848| 
00849| <AppOnly>
00850| 
00851| The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport.
00852| 
00853| However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element. If you'd like to disable this behavior, you can pass `scroll={false}` to the `<Link>` component, or `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
00854| 
00855| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00856| import Link from 'next/link'
00857| 
00858| export default function Page() {
00859|   return (
00860|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00861|       Disables scrolling to the top
00862|     </Link>
00863|   )
00864| }
00865| ```
00866| 
00867| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00868| import Link from 'next/link'
00869| 
00870| export default function Page() {
00871|   return (
00872|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00873|       Disables scrolling to the top
00874|     </Link>
00875|   )
00876| }
00877| ```
00878| 
00879| Using `router.push()` or `router.replace()`:
00880| 
00881| ```jsx
00882| // useRouter
00883| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00884| 
00885| const router = useRouter()
00886| 
00887| router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })
00888| ```
00889| 
00890| </AppOnly>
00891| 
00892| <PagesOnly>
00893| 
00894| The default behavior of `Link` is to scroll to the top of the page. When there is a hash defined it will scroll to the specific id, like a normal `<a>` tag. To prevent scrolling to the top / hash `scroll={false}` can be added to `Link`:

00922| ### Scroll offset with sticky headers
00923| 
00924| Because Next.js skips sticky and fixed positioned elements when finding the scroll target, content may end up behind a sticky header after navigation. For example, if your layout has a sticky header:
00925| 
00926| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

`<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.

Basic usage:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

00230| ### `scroll`
00231| 
00232| **Defaults to `true`.** The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport. However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element.
00233| 
00234| When `scroll = {false}`, Next.js will not attempt to scroll to the first Page element.
00235| 
00236| > **Good to know**: Next.js checks if `scroll: false` before managing scroll behavior. If scrolling is enabled, it identifies the relevant DOM node for navigation and inspects each top-level element. All non-scrollable elements and those without rendered HTML are bypassed, this includes sticky or fixed positioned elements, and non-visible elements such as those calculated with `getBoundingClientRect`. Next.js then continues through siblings until it identifies a scrollable element that is visible in the viewport.

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00304| - `false`: Prefetching will never happen both on entering the viewport and on hover.
00305| 
00306| > **With Partial Prefetching enabled** ([`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching)): the default changes. `auto` prefetches the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) (the route's static and cached content) instead of the full page. See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the full behavior change.
00307| 
00308| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00309| import Link from 'next/link'
00310| 
00311| export default function Page() {
00312|   return (
00313|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00314|       Dashboard
00315|     </Link>
00316|   )
00317| }
00318| ```
00319| 
00320| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00321| import Link from 'next/link'
00322| 
00323| export default function Page() {

00325|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00326|       Dashboard
00327|     </Link>
00328|   )
00329| }
00330| ```
00331| 
00332| </AppOnly>

00453| ### `onNavigate`
00454| 
00455| An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a `preventDefault()` method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed.
00456| 
00457| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00458| import Link from 'next/link'
00459| 
00460| export default function Page() {
00461|   return (
00462|     <Link
00463|       href="/dashboard"
00464|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00465|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00466|         console.log('Navigating...')
00467| 
00468|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00469|         // e.preventDefault()
00470|       }}
00471|     >
00472|       Dashboard
00473|     </Link>
00474|   )
00475| }
00476| ```
00477| 
00478| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00479| import Link from 'next/link'
00480| 
00481| export default function Page() {
00482|   return (
00483|     <Link
00484|       href="/dashboard"
00485|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00486|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00487|         console.log('Navigating...')
00488| 
00489|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00490|         // e.preventDefault()
00491|       }}
00492|     >
00493|       Dashboard
00494|     </Link>
00495|   )
00496| }
00497| ```
00498| 
00499| > **Good to know**: While `onClick` and `onNavigate` may seem similar, they serve different purposes. `onClick` executes for all click events, while `onNavigate` only runs during client-side navigation. Some key differences:
00500| >
00501| > - When using modifier keys (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` + Click), `onClick` executes but `onNavigate` doesn't since Next.js prevents default navigation for new tabs.
00502| > - External URLs won't trigger `onNavigate` since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.
00503| > - Links with the `download` attribute will work with `onClick` but not `onNavigate` since the browser will treat the linked URL as a download.

00537| ## Examples

00541| <AppOnly>
00542| 
00543| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00544| 
00545| When linking to [dynamic segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can use [template literals and interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) to generate a list of links. For example, to generate a list of blog posts:
00546| 
00547| ```tsx filename="app/blog/post-list.tsx" switcher

00549| 
00550| interface Post {
00551|   id: number
00552|   title: string
00553|   slug: string
00554| }
00555| 
00556| export default function PostList({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
00557|   return (
00558|     <ul>
00559|       {posts.map((post) => (
00560|         <li key={post.id}>
00561|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00562|         </li>
00563|       ))}
00564|     </ul>
00565|   )
00566| }
00567| ```

00847| ### Disable scrolling to the top of the page
00848| 
00849| <AppOnly>
00850| 
00851| The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport.
00852| 
00853| However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element. If you'd like to disable this behavior, you can pass `scroll={false}` to the `<Link>` component, or `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
00854| 
00855| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00856| import Link from 'next/link'
00857| 
00858| export default function Page() {

00974| ### Prefetching links in Proxy
00975| 
00976| It's common to use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) for authentication or other purposes that involve rewriting the user to a different page. In order for the `<Link />` component to properly prefetch links with rewrites via Proxy, you need to tell Next.js both the URL to display and the URL to prefetch. 00986|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
00987|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
00988|     } else {
00989|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))

00992| }

00230| ### `scroll`
00231| 
00232| **Defaults to `true`.** The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport. However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element.
00233| 
00234| When `scroll = {false}`, Next.js will not attempt to scroll to the first Page element.
00235| 
00236| > **Good to know**: Next.js checks if `scroll: false` before managing scroll behavior. If scrolling is enabled, it identifies the relevant DOM node for navigation and inspects each top-level element. All non-scrollable elements and those without rendered HTML are bypassed, this includes sticky or fixed positioned elements, and non-visible elements such as those calculated with `getBoundingClientRect`. Next.js then continues through siblings until it identifies a scrollable element that is visible in the viewport.

00247|     </Link>

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00304| - `false`: Prefetching will never happen both on entering the viewport and on hover.
00305| 
00306| > **With Partial Prefetching enabled** ([`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching)): the default changes. `auto` prefetches the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) (the route's static and cached content) instead of the full page. See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the full behavior change.
00307| 
00308| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00309| import Link from 'next/link'
00310| 
00311| export default function Page() {
00312|   return (
00313|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00314|       Dashboard
00315|     </Link>
00316|   )
00317| }
00318| ```
00319| 
00320| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00321| import Link from 'next/link'
00322| 
00323| export default function Page() {
00324|   return (
00325|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00326|       Dashboard
00327|     </Link>
00328|   )
00329| }
00330| ```
00331| 
00332| </AppOnly>
00333|

00453| ### `onNavigate`
00454| 
00455| An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a `preventDefault()` method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed.
00456| 
00457| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00458| import Link from 'next/link'
00459| 
00460| export default function Page() {
00461|   return (
00462|     <Link
00463|       href="/dashboard"
00464|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00465|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00466|         console.log('Navigating...')
00467| 
00468|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00469|         // e.preventDefault()
00470|       }}
00471|     >
00472|       Dashboard
00473|     </Link>
00474|   )
00475| }
00476| ```
00477| 
00478| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00479| import Link from 'next/link'
00480| 
00481| export default function Page() {
00482|   return (
00483|     <Link
00484|       href="/dashboard"
00485|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00486|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00487|         console.log('Navigating...')
00488| 
00489|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00490|         // e.preventDefault()
00491|       }}
00492|     >
00493|       Dashboard
00494|     </Link>
00495|   )
00496| }
00497| ```
00498| 
00499| > **Good to know**: While `onClick` and `onNavigate` may seem similar, they serve different purposes. `onClick` executes for all click events, while `onNavigate` only runs during client-side navigation. Some key differences:
00500| >
00501| > - When using modifier keys (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` + Click), `onClick` executes but `onNavigate` doesn't since Next.js prevents default navigation for new tabs.
00502| > - External URLs won't trigger `onNavigate` since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.
00503| > - Links with the `download` attribute will work with `onClick` but not `onNavigate` since the browser will treat the linked URL as a download.

00537| ## Examples
00538| 
00539| The following examples demonstrate how to use the `<Link>` component in different scenarios.

00541| <AppOnly>
00542| 
00543| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00544| 
00545| When linking to [dynamic segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can use [template literals and interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) to generate a list of links. For example, to generate a list of blog posts:
00546| 
00547| ```tsx filename="app/blog/post-list.tsx" switcher
00548| import Link from 'next/link'
00549| 
00550| interface Post {
00551|   id: number
00552|   title: string
00553|   slug: string
00554| }
00555| 
00556| export default function PostList({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
00557|   return (
00558|     <ul>
00559|       {posts.map((post) => (
00560|         <li key={post.id}>
00561|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00562|         </li>
00563|       ))}
00564|     </ul>
00565|   )
00566| }
00567| ```
00568| 
00569| ```jsx filename="app/blog/post-list.js" switcher

00573|   return (

00577|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00578|         </li>
00579|       ))}
00580|     </ul>
00581|   )
00582| }
00583| ```
